rows.sub_theme: National power-system expansion and decarbonisation pathways (SIN and economy-wide scenarios)
rows.methods: Study types: modelling-simulation 12; techno-economic-assessment 1. Named techniques in method field (keyword matches): optimisation/least-cost/programming 5; GCAM/TIMES/OSeMOSYS/Calliope/TIAM 2; LEAP 1; expert panels/surveys/interviews/workshops 1; econometrics/statistics 1
rows.settings: Sectors: power-generation-SIN 10; multi-sector 3. Departments: national/no department 13
rows.technical: 2050 power capacity 127-170 GW [R0074]; electricity share 54-69% [R0074]; installed capacity 18 to 41 GW (+127%), renewables 84.14% of capacity [R0267]; ISO case 13.2 GW solar and 10.73 GW wind added, RO case 37.84 GW solar PV and 2.13 GW wind [R0285]; 15.5-16.1 GW solar, 6.4 GW wind [R0491]; solar and wind 23-26% of generation and 45-55% of capacity [R0646]; hydropower capacity factor cut 5.5-17.1% by climate change [R0324]; minimum reserve margin 11% [R0079]
rows.economic: net benefit US$70 bn (21.2% of 2021 GDP, DPS) [R0074]; average price USD 55/MWh vs 65 [R0079]; investment 0.81-0.93 vs 1.72-1.73 M USD/MW for traditional [R0491]; USD 123-267 billion (36-77% of GDP), 3.6-7.8 times the government's USD 34 billion [R0488]; tax reduction adds only 2% capacity at 4.75 billion USD cost [R0258]; expected cost from about 22.4 to 24.6 billion USD [R0324]; LCOE 1.17-1.60 USD/kWh versus 0.018-0.035 in SCN 2-3 [R0319]
rows.environmental: 2050 emissions 7 MtCO2e (DPS) vs 177.3 BAU [R0074]; CO2 44 Mtoe vs 145 for BAU [R0079]; 331,808 t CO2 vs 1,094,349 t [R0267]; emissions fall 21.2% (direct tax), 13.3% (indirect tax), 37.7% (FIT) and 41.9% (combined) [R0527]; CO2 2030: 108.3 vs 118.5 Mton [R0023]
rows.pattern: Scenario studies agree on large renewable additions but differ widely in scale (installed capacity 18 to 41 GW (+127%) in R0267; solar and wind 23-26% of generation in R0646; 13.2 GW solar in the ISO case and 37.84 GW in the RO case of R0285; 15.5-16.1 GW solar in R0491). Emission and cost outcomes use different baselines and units (2050 emissions 7 MtCO2e versus 177.3 BAU in R0074; emissions fall 21.2% to 41.9% across tax and FIT scenarios in R0527; net benefit US$70 bn in R0074 versus USD 123-267 billion in R0488), so values are not directly comparable.

rows.sub_theme: Renewable resource potential, complementarity and multi-criteria selection or hybrid design for regions and non-interconnected zones
rows.methods: Study types: modelling-simulation 7; empirical-case-study 1; other 1; techno-economic-assessment 1. Named techniques in method field (keyword matches): multi-criteria (AHP/TOPSIS/ANP) 5; expert panels/surveys/interviews/workshops 5; optimisation/least-cost/programming 2; literature/document review 1; GIS/spatial 1
rows.settings: Sectors: power-generation-SIN 6; non-interconnected-zones 4. Departments: Norte de Santander 1; Bolívar 1; Valle del Cauca 1; San Andrés y Providencia 1; Chocó 1; Meta 1; Putumayo 1; national/no department 5
rows.technical: wind speed 2.6-4.7 m/s [R0087]; solar >11,000 TWh/year, wind 35 GW and 176 TWh/year [R0209]; VRE-hydro capacity ratio 44% [R0252]; PV ranks first or near-top in most scenarios (TOPSIS 30.19% Caribbean 1; fuzzy 29%), Andean large hydro 29.55% (TOPSIS), 30% (fuzzy) [R0006]; best alternative 50% solar + 50% biomass [R0124]; A10 capacities PV 25 kW, wind 15 kW, biomass 7 kW, diesel 4 kW [R0045]; 5,772 kW PV and 12,892 kW wind [R0128]
rows.economic: CAPEX 0.86-1.1 MUSD/MW (solar) and 1.57-1.88 MUSD/MW (wind) [R0209]; Riosucio NPV US$3,618,837 (subsidized, PV) [R0537]; profit -159,470 USD (A1) to -121,360 USD (A10) [R0045]; total present value 292.58 million USD [R0128]
rows.environmental: CO2 1718.98 million kg (5.80% saving) [R0128]; 245.88 t CO2 (A1) and 94.72 t CO2 (A10) [R0045]; AHP weights intervened area 48.3%, species affectation 27.2% [R0352]
rows.pattern: Resource assessments show potential (wind speed 2.6-4.7 m/s in R0087; solar >11,000 TWh/year and wind 35 GW in R0209; VRE-hydro capacity ratio 44% in R0252), while multi-criteria studies (R0006, R0484, R0352) rank alternatives by criteria weights that depend on the expert panel (PV ranks first or near-top in most scenarios in R0006). Design and optimisation studies (R0045, R0124, R0128, R0537) report site-specific results (profit -159,470 USD (A1) to -121,360 USD (A10) in R0045; total present value 292.58 million USD in R0128; Riosucio NPV US$3,618,837 in R0537) that are not comparable across studies.

rows.sub_theme: Economics, incentives, policy, institutions and social/territorial dimensions of the energy transition
rows.methods: Study types: policy-analysis 3; techno-economic-assessment 2; modelling-simulation 1; empirical-case-study 1. Named techniques in method field (keyword matches): expert panels/surveys/interviews/workshops 3; optimisation/least-cost/programming 2; econometrics/statistics 1; Monte Carlo/DCF 1
rows.settings: Sectors: power-generation-SIN 4; buildings-residential 2; multi-sector 1. Departments: national/no department 7
rows.economic: fiscal incentives alone cut generation cost 7.74-13.25% [R0419]; tax incentives alone cut cost only 3.7-8.7% [R0454]; generation cost reductions of 22.6% (FB, 0.072 USD/kWh), 36.7% (USW, 0.088), 49.2% (PV, 0.032) and 49.1% (WP, 0.058) with optimal structure [R0454]; mean marginal cost 9.5 US cents/kWh [R0280]; 95 plants, 643 MW of small hydro under capacity mechanisms [R0507]
rows.environmental: ERE for climate change 1.9-8.2% [R0004]; savings 12.93 (wind) and 10.18 (solar) g CO2-Eq/kWh [R0004]
rows.pattern: Financial studies show that incentives lower generation cost (fiscal incentives alone cut 7.74-13.25% in R0419; tax incentives alone only 3.7-8.7% in R0454, with reductions of up to 49.2% under an optimal structure), R0280 estimates a mean marginal cost of 9.5 US cents/kWh, R0507 documents capacity mechanisms (95 plants, 643 MW of small hydro), and R0004 reports savings of 12.93 (wind) and 10.18 (solar) g CO2-Eq/kWh. R0455 (analytic network process) and R1612 (practitioner workshops) are expert-based and contribute no values to this table; no technical outcomes are reported.

rows.settings: Sectors: transport 3; multi-sector 3; industry 2; power-generation-SIN 1. Departments: Santander 1; national/no department 8
rows.technical: empty trips 59.49% [R0354]; electrolysis efficiency 60-80% [R0223]; R/P 5.9 years, domestic gas covers 100% of demand only until 2H 2026 [R0935]; national VI 8.64 of max 20 [R0431]; 100 incentives identified [R0237]
rows.economic: investments US$6900 M to 2030 and US$26,700 M to 2050 [R0250]; annual capital costs 0.5-4% of GDP [R0250]; theoretical potential 22 Mt CO2/y at 196 EUR/t average cost [R0246]; 36% of industrial energy lost (USD 6.6 billion) [R0223]; about 10.30 USD/kg [R0223]
rows.environmental: avoid 8% (58.3 Mt CO2eq) of cumulative BAU emissions to 2030 and 18% to 2050 [R0250]; CO2e reduction of 13% by 2030 and 47% by 2050 [R0354]; reduce 106% and 98% of refinery emissions but only ~13% of life-cycle emissions [R0246]; renewable energy -0.47% CO2 [R0434]
rows.pattern: Mitigation estimates vary with method and baseline: R0250 avoids 8% (58.3 Mt CO2eq) of cumulative BAU emissions to 2030 and 18% to 2050, R0354 reports CO2e reductions of 13% by 2030 and 47% by 2050 from fleet renewal, R0246 gives a theoretical potential of 22 Mt CO2/y at 196 EUR/t, and the econometric R0434 finds renewable energy -0.47% CO2. R0223 and R0935 add sector-specific figures (36% of industrial energy lost; R/P 5.9 years for gas), but metrics differ and are not directly comparable.
